summary: All seven 3.6 items were traced to concrete code. Items 1 and 6a share one root cause: LmdbStorageEstimatorEvidence gates B-tree/exact storage evidence on the *existence* of the statistics service (`statistics == null` at :162, `statistics != null` at :269, `mappedStatisticsOwnPlanning()` at :311) instead of on whether Frontier actually answered in AUTHORITATIVE mode, so any typed Frontier fallback (NO_GENERATION, CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE, GENERATION_TOO_STALE, MEMORY_PRESSURE) leaves the resolver with zero candidates and `heuristic(1.0)`; SHADOW mode removes the same evidence. The fix is a single "Frontier answered authoritatively" predicate plus the roadmap 4.3 fallback chain (Frontier -> bounded page/B-tree estimate -> exact count only in the decision tier -> total-rows ceiling), extracted into a small helper because the class sits at 697/700 lines. Items 2 and 3 are scheduler-policy defects in LmdbSailStore: deterministic delta failures (persistent-envelope MEMORY_PRESSURE, Omni dimension IOException) are mapped to RETRY forever (:1254-1263) and RETRY returns before the base rebuild (:1169-1172); the quiet period is a debounce with no deadline that every commit resets (:1137, :1436-1439). Fixes: typed permanent-failure classification with bounded retries and a delta-tier insertion-debt trigger that folds deltas into a new base before the envelope is hit; a maximum-deferral deadline for the quiet period. Item 4 needs a reference-count-aware retirement GC in LmdbStatisticsService/FrontierStatisticsManifestStore that keeps current + predecessor. Item 5 is an orientation-selection bug in FrontierOmniIndex.estimateJoin (:246-259) that accepts a weak zero-witness forward bridge; item 6b is the absence of any per-estimate work bound on bridge scans (leaves and paths already have one). Item 7's stale-generation window is confirmed by code reading and gets a precise acquire() guard; the AGMS bound and quad-synopsis races could not be reproduced and get a small guard / deferral respectively.

findings.title: Cold start / stale Frontier -> 1-row leaf estimates (unknown collapses to 1)
findings.recommendationReason: Confirmed by repro and e2e (datagovbe >60 s); every other lifecycle failure in 3.6 degrades into this 1-row state, so fixing it caps the blast radius of 3.6.2/3.6.3/3.6.7a. The fix is a precise gate change plus the roadmap 4.3 fallback chain; no optimisation is disabled.
findings.rootCause: core/sail/lmdb/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/sail/lmdb/LmdbStorageEstimatorEvidence.java:147-165 `statementCandidates`: the Frontier SYNOPSIS candidate is added only when `statisticsMode == AUTHORITATIVE && estimate.fallbackReason() == NONE && valid(point)` (:151-158), but the STORAGE_SUMMARY candidate is gated by `cardinalities != null && statistics == null` (:162) — i.e. on the *existence* of the service, not on whether it answered. `exactCandidate` (:268-270) likewise returns empty whenever `statistics != null`. With Frontier AUTHORITATIVE and NO_GENERATION (cold start), GENERATION_TOO_STALE, CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE (tail cleared after a >16 384-mutation txn, LmdbStatisticsService.installMutationTail/appendMutationTail :488-556) or MEMORY_PRESSURE, `leafCandidates` returns `[]`. EstimateEvidenceResolver.resolve (:36-45) then returns `BagEstimate.heuristic(1.0, "no-current-evidence")` with interval [0, MAX] and confidence 0. Packed path reaches the same code: LmdbPackedCostModel.estimateRows (:212-220) -> `mappedLeafEstimate` is null when not READY -> `legacyEstimateRows` (:223-241) -> because `runtime.statisticsService() != null` it calls `runtime.conventionalStatementPatternRows(pattern)` (LmdbEstimatorRuntime :437-440) -> `estimate()` -> LmdbEstimationEngine.resolvedLeaf (:463-466) -> same resolver -> 1.0. LmdbEstimatorStorageAccess.packedStatementPatternRows (:92-109) also returns `Double.NaN` in AUTHORITATIVE whenever `fallbackReason != NONE` instead of `legacyPackedRows` (finite-probe path LmdbPackedCostModel:3592-3600). The B-tree page estimator (TripleStore.cardinality/planningCardinality :1754-1803, bounded, cached per dataRevision in LmdbStatementPatternCardinalitySource.estimateIds :267-286) is available the whole time and is exactly the roadmap's 'B-tree range count' tier.
findings.fix: Introduce one predicate and one fallback chain, implemented once and used by both pipelines. (1) New package-private helper `LmdbFrontierLeafAnswer` (new file, needed because LmdbStorageEstimatorEvidence is at 697 lines against LmdbEstimatorArchitectureTest.MAX_IMPLEMENTATION_LINES=700; add it to ROOT_IMPLEMENTATIONS): `static boolean answered(FrontierEstimatorMode mode, FrontierLeafEstimate e)` = `mode == AUTHORITATIVE && e != null && e.fallbackReason() == NONE && valid(e.pointRows())`. (2) LmdbStorageEstimatorEvidence.statementCandidates: compute `FrontierLeafEstimate frontier = frontierProbe == null ? null : statistics.estimateLeafCurrent(frontierProbe)` once; `boolean frontierAnswered = LmdbFrontierLeafAnswer.answered(statisticsMode, frontier)`; add the SYNOPSIS candidate when answered (unchanged); change the storage gate at :162 to `cardinalities != null && !frontierAnswered` so the bounded page estimate is a STORAGE_SUMMARY candidate (source `lmdb-storage-summary`, confidence 0.55, interval [rows/2, 2·rows]) whenever Frontier did not answer; append the fallback reason to the source string (e.g. `lmdb-storage-summary/frontier-NO_GENERATION`) so explain output shows why. (3) Pessimistic ceiling (roadmap 4.3 last tier): if `cardinalities != null && !frontierAnswered` and the summary itself is invalid (-1/NaN), add a HEURISTIC candidate with rows = `cardinalities.estimateForPlanning(new StatementPattern(?s ?p ?o))` (total rows, cached per dataRevision), lower 0, upper = same, confidence 0.0, source `lmdb-unknown-ceiling`; a StatementPattern leaf therefore never resolves to 1 row when storage exists. (4) `exactCandidate` (:268-270): replace `|| statistics != null` with `|| frontierLeafAnswered(pattern)` (helper that re-probes `estimateLeafCurrent`; cheap — tail overlay or generation lookup; optionally memoise per EstimateContext). The exact tier stays behind `resolveForDecision`'s `exactProbePermitted && tier.allowsExactEstimates()` (EstimateEvidenceResolver :47-58), so no new unbounded `TripleStore.exactCardinality` scans (:2105-2117) are introduced on the STANDARD tier. (5) LmdbEstimatorStorageAccess.packedStatementPatternRows (:100-104): in AUTHORITATIVE return `legacyPackedRows(...)` when `estimate.fallbackReason() != NONE` (and when `probe == null`, which means an unresolvable constant → legacy returns exact 0) instead of NaN. Soundness: storage evidence is only consulted when Frontier explicitly declined, so every existing 'Frontier answered => never touch LMDB cardinalities' contract is preserved (verified: LmdbEstimatorStorageAccessV2Test, LmdbFrontierV2EstimatorEvidenceTest, LmdbFrontierPlanningIntegrationTest all await READY or mock fallbackReason NONE).

findings.title: SHADOW mode changes planning evidence (drops storage-summary, exact and filter evidence)
findings.recommendationReason: Same gate defect as 3.6.1 and lands as part of the same helper; SHADOW is documented as observation-only, so removing planner evidence violates its contract.
findings.rootCause: LmdbStorageEstimatorEvidence: `frontierProbe()` (:232-236) returns a probe for any mode != OFF, so SHADOW calls `estimateLeafCurrent` (observation, correct) but never adds a candidate (mode != AUTHORITATIVE, :151); yet the STORAGE_SUMMARY gate `statistics == null` (:162) and the exact gate `statistics != null` (:269) are mode-blind, so SHADOW removes both. Additionally `mappedStatisticsOwnPlanning()` (:311-313) is `statistics != null && statisticsMode != OFF`, so in SHADOW `filterEvidence` (:281-308) is routed to `mappedFilters.estimate` and the exact bounded-zero probe path is skipped — SHADOW also changes filter evidence. Repro: OFF -> [STORAGE_SUMMARY:250000]+exact, SHADOW -> [] no exact.
findings.fix: Define `private boolean authoritative()` = `statistics != null && statisticsMode == AUTHORITATIVE` and use it in the three gates: (a) :162 `cardinalities != null && !frontierAnswered` (frontierAnswered is already false in SHADOW because `LmdbFrontierLeafAnswer.answered` requires AUTHORITATIVE); (b) :269 exact gate via the same predicate; (c) :311 `mappedStatisticsOwnPlanning()` -> `authoritative()`. Keep the SHADOW observation call (`estimateLeafCurrent`) so telemetry is unchanged. Result: SHADOW evidence == OFF evidence for leaves, exact and filters, plus observation.

findings.title: Delta publication stalls forever at the delta envelope; failures map to RETRY and never escalate to a base rebuild; -Xmx drift causes permanent dimension mismatch
findings.recommendationReason: Confirmed at both 16 MiB and the 512 MiB default (stalls after 112 000 inserted statements, restart does not recover). A store that stops publishing degrades to CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE -> GENERATION_TOO_STALE and, without 3.6.1, to 1-row plans permanently.
findings.rootCause: (a) LmdbSailStore.refreshFrontierStatisticsDelta (:1203-1264): `catch (FrontierStatisticsException)` (:1254-1259) escalates only `CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE`; every other typed failure, including `MEMORY_PRESSURE` from FrontierStatisticsDeltaBuilder.validateDiskBudget (:247-261, "exceeds its persistent envelope") and `catch (IOException)` (:1260-1263), returns RETRY. runScheduledFrontierRebuild (:1157-1200) returns on RETRY (:1169-1172) *before* the base-rebuild branch, and the `finally` reschedules (:1191-1199) every `estimatorPersistDelayMillis` (1 s) — the identical, deterministic failure repeats forever. (b) The envelope is structural: FrontierStatisticsBuildConfig.forDiskBudget (:73-94) sets `delta = disk - disk/8 - disk/4 - disk/4 - 5·disk/16 = disk/16` (32 MiB at the 512 MiB default); FrontierStatisticsDeltaCompactor merges layer families but retains every mutation (~300 B/mutation observed), so the delta tier grows monotonically with inserts since the last base and the envelope is a hard ceiling on mutations-since-base. Nothing triggers a base rebuild before the ceiling (only `deleteDebt >= 0.10` at :1248 and 'transaction exceeds the bounded batch' at :1235). (c) Budget drift: LmdbStoreConfig.FRONTIER_HEAP_BUDGET_BYTES = `Runtime.getRuntime().maxMemory() / 4` (:83); FrontierStatisticsBuildConfig.forBudgets (:100-160) halves `cellCount` (the Omni width) under heap pressure (:147-152); FrontierOmniDeltaBuilder.build (:64-69) throws a plain `IOException` when the base layout's width/depth/lanes differ from the *current* config — deterministic, caught as IOException -> RETRY forever after a JVM restart with a different -Xmx. (d) Meanwhile the in-memory tail is cleared once uncovered mutations exceed MAXIMUM_IN_MEMORY_MUTATIONS=16 384 (LmdbSailStore.appendCurrentFrontierMutationTail :1303-1331), so leaves fall to CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE and, after `maximumLagMillis` (60 s), GENERATION_TOO_STALE.
findings.fix: Three independent parts. (1) Typed permanence: add `boolean permanent` to FrontierStatisticsException (new ctor + `requiresBaseRebuild()`), set it in FrontierStatisticsDeltaBuilder.validateDiskBudget (:257-259), the layer-limit throw (:204-206), the dimension-overflow throw (:225-227), and convert FrontierOmniDeltaBuilder's dimension mismatch (:64-69) from `IOException` to `FrontierStatisticsException(SHARD_CORRUPT, permanent=true)`. In LmdbSailStore.refreshFrontierStatisticsDelta replace the catch logic with `classifyDeltaFailure(Throwable)` (static, unit-testable): permanent or CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE -> BASE_REBUILD_REQUIRED; otherwise RETRY but bounded: keep `consecutiveDeltaRetries`/`lastDeltaRetryCoveredSequence` fields, and after FRONTIER_MAX_DELTA_RETRIES (8) consecutive RETRYs for the same covered sequence escalate to BASE_REBUILD_REQUIRED and log once at WARN (transient heap-governor refusals and I/O errors therefore cannot pin the store either). Reset the counter on COMPLETE or a successful publish. (2) Insertion-debt trigger (roadmap 'staleness-aware deltas'): in refreshFrontierStatisticsDelta, before building and after a successful publish, if `service.status().diskBytesByTier().get(DELTAS_AND_MANIFESTS) >= FRONTIER_DELTA_TIER_REBUILD_FRACTION (0.75) * statisticsBuildConfig.deltaAndManifestBudgetBytes()` -> return BASE_REBUILD_REQUIRED (mirrors the existing deleteDebt trigger at :1248). Base rebuilds fold all deltas into a fresh base so the envelope failure becomes exceptional instead of the steady state; this is what makes `defaultBudgetInsertOnlyGrowthKeepsFrontierCurrent` pass without ever hitting the exception path. (3) Dimension check at open: in LmdbSailStore init (:432-451) after `LmdbStatisticsService.open`, if `status.availability()==READY` and the current manifest's `width()/depth()/designLaneCount()/auditLaneCount()` differ from `statisticsBuildConfig.cellCount()/omniDepth()/designLaneCount()/auditLaneCount()`, set a `frontierDimensionRebuildRequired` flag that `refreshFrontierStatisticsDelta` treats like `service.rebuildRequired()` (BASE_REBUILD_REQUIRED at :1209) and `requestFrontierRebuild()`; clear it after a successful base rebuild. Preferred longer-term: derive the delta config from the manifest (`FrontierStatisticsBuildConfig.withOmniDimensions(width, depth)`) when the heap governor admits it, so a restart with less heap does not force a rebuild — optional follow-up.

findings.title: Base rebuild starvation: quiet period is reset by every commit with no deadline
findings.recommendationReason: Confirmed: covered sequence stays 0 for 12 s under 4 commits/s while the 20 000-row predicate is estimated as 1 row. A steady trickle of writes is a normal production workload.
findings.rootCause: LmdbSailStore.flush commit path (:2358-2367) calls `requestFrontierRebuild()` on every commit, which sets `frontierRebuildRequestedNanos = System.nanoTime()` (:1136-1139). runScheduledFrontierRebuild (:1174-1177) only starts a base rebuild when `frontierRebuildQuietPeriodElapsed()` (:1436-1439: ≥ estimatorPersistDelayMillis = 1 000 ms since the *last* request) and no write txn is active; otherwise RETRY. The `finally` block (:1185-1187) also forces retry whenever the request timestamp moved during the run. With ≥1 commit/s the debounce never expires — there is no upper bound on deferral. Because the 20 k-statement transaction exceeded MAXIMUM_IN_MEMORY_MUTATIONS the tail was cleared (:1303-1331) and `completeTransactionPrefix` returned empty (:1333-1343 -> BASE_REBUILD_REQUIRED), so the only path to coverage is the starved base rebuild; leaves stay CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE (LmdbStatisticsService.currentFallbackReason :884-895) -> 1 row. Secondary (plausible, code-read): LmdbPackedCostModel.mappedStatisticsReady (:407-414) requires `status.fallbackReason()==NONE`, which is false between any commit and its delta publication even when the in-memory tail fully covers the commit, so the packed session flips mapped/scalar every commit for ~1 s.
findings.fix: Turn the debounce into debounce-with-deadline. Add `volatile long frontierBaseRebuildPendingSinceNanos` (0 when none). Set it (if 0) whenever runScheduledFrontierRebuild determines a base rebuild is required (after `refreshFrontierStatisticsDelta` returns BASE_REBUILD_REQUIRED, or `service.rebuildRequired()`); clear it after `rebuildFrontierStatisticsV2()` returns true. Replace the gate at :1174 with `!(frontierRebuildQuietPeriodElapsed() || baseRebuildDeferralExceeded()) || storeTxnStarted.get()` where `baseRebuildDeferralExceeded()` = `pendingSince != 0 && now - pendingSince >= FRONTIER_REBUILD_MAX_DEFERRAL_NANOS` (5 s). Extract the policy into a tiny package-private `FrontierRebuildSchedulePolicy.shouldStartBaseRebuild(now, lastRequest, pendingSince, quietNanos, maxDeferralNanos)` for unit testing. The snapshot-based rebuild is safe while commits continue (LMDB MVCC; later mutations are covered by deltas), so the deadline changes only *when* the rebuild starts. Keep the `storeTxnStarted` guard unchanged (see open question). For the mapped/scalar flip (secondary): expose `LmdbStatisticsService.currentEstimatesAvailable()` = `currentFallbackReason()==NONE || hasCompleteMutationTail()` and let `mappedStatisticsReady()` use it — but the view path (`openCurrentView`) does not apply the tail, so this must be paired with tail-aware views; recommend deferring that part to a follow-up (it is a plan-stability improvement, not a correctness fix).

findings.title: Superseded manifests and shards are never deleted (unbounded disk growth)
findings.recommendationReason: Every delta publication leaves a manifest plus 6+ shard files behind (12 commits -> 13 manifests, 150 shards, 3.2x live bytes); with 3.6.2's proactive base rebuilds the growth rate would increase, so GC should land with or before it.
findings.rootCause: LmdbStatisticsService.publish (:84-125) opens the new generation, calls FrontierStatisticsManifestStore.publish (:58-88: writes `manifest-<gen>.fs2m`, `switchCurrent`) and only `old.release()`s the previous generation (unmap). FrontierStatisticsDeltaBuilder writes 3 scalar + 3 Omni shard files per delta (plus compaction outputs); FrontierStatisticsDeltaCompactor.compact deletes only files whose `ownerGenerationId == generationId` of the *current* build (:collectUnpublished), so layers merged away that were owned by earlier generations remain. FrontierStatisticsBuilder base rebuilds leave the entire previous base. The only deleters are recovery paths (`discardGeneration` :138-168, `resetOwnedArtifacts` :174) and `cleanupTemporaryArtifacts` (temporaries only). Shards are shared across generations by fileName (delta manifests carry the base's descriptors with `ownerGenerationId` set, :192-197 of the delta builder), so deletion must be by live-file-set difference, not by owner.
findings.fix: Reference-count-aware retirement GC. (1) FrontierStatisticsManifestStore: add `synchronized void retireSuperseded(Set<Long> retainedGenerationIds, Set<String> liveFileNames)`: list the directory; delete every published `MANIFEST_FILE` whose generation is not retained and every published `SHARD_FILE` whose name is not in `liveFileNames` (never `.tmp`, never CURRENT); `forceDirectory`. (2) LmdbStatisticsService: retention policy = current manifest + its direct predecessor (`previousGenerationId`), because `rollback()` (:141-162) and `recoverInvalidGeneration` (:741-795) load the predecessor. Maintain `List<FrontierStatisticsGeneration> retired` (generations replaced by publish/rollback that may still be leased). Add `FrontierStatisticsGeneration.onFullyReleased(Runnable)` invoked in `release()` when the count hits 0 (:283-291). In `publish` after `installGeneration`: push `old` to `retired`, register the hook, then call `collectGarbage()`. `collectGarbage()` (synchronized): liveFiles = files(current) ∪ files(load(current.previous) if exists) ∪ files(g) for every g in `retired` with refcount > 0; retainedGens = {current, current.previous} ∪ {g.generationId : g retired and still referenced}; call `retireSuperseded`. The hook simply schedules `collectGarbage()` (may run on the releasing thread; it is I/O light). (3) Startup: in `loadPublishedGeneration` after a successful `installGeneration` (:719-725) call `collectGarbage()` (nothing is leased yet) so directories bloated by the current code are cleaned on first open. (4) `discardGeneration`/`resetOwnedArtifacts` unchanged. Deleting only unmapped files keeps Windows semantics safe; on POSIX lingering readers would be fine anyway.

findings.title: Omni bridge returns a weak zero-witness forward estimate instead of trying the reverse orientation
findings.recommendationReason: Confirmed: exact 160 000 estimated as 0 (conf 0) while the reverse orientation gives 164 860. A point 0 with fallbackReason NONE is treated as knowledge by every consumer (LmdbPackedCostModel costs pointRows regardless of confidence), producing catastrophic plans on hub-shaped data.
findings.rootCause: FrontierOmniIndex.estimateJoin (:246-259): the forward `estimateBridge`/`estimateCompositeBridge` result is returned whenever `fallbackReason() == NONE`; the reverse orientation is evaluated only when forward is *unavailable*. `sampledJoinEstimate` (:1331-1359) returns weak ensembles (`quality.isWeak` -> `point, lower 0, upper productBound, confidence≈0`) with fallbackReason NONE, so a forward bridge whose sampled lanes never hit the hub (8 hub rows among 20 000 on the sampled side: every lane point 0, sharedWitnesses 0, `FrontierSamplingQuality.confidence()`==0) is 'available' with point 0. FrontierMappedStatistics.estimateJoin (:455-478) prefers `centers` only when they are available; when `centers.estimateJoin` is unavailable it returns the weak omni zero (:476-478). Existing contract test `sparseSingletonBridgeDoesNotTreatMissingWitnessAsAuthoritativeZero` already states that a sampled zero must yield to calibrated evidence — the orientation choice violates it when centers are absent.
findings.fix: In FrontierOmniIndex.estimateJoin (both branches): compute `forward`; if `forward` is exact (confidence 1.0 / `exactBridgeEstimate`) return it; otherwise compute `reverse` (transposed pairs for the composite case) and select deterministically with a private `preferBridge(a, b)`: (1) available beats unavailable; (2) exact beats sampled; (3) strong (not weak) beats weak — expose weakness by returning a small private record `BridgeResult(FrontierJoinEstimate estimate, long sharedWitnesses, boolean weak)` from `sampledJoinEstimate`/`estimateBridge`; (4) among two weak results prefer more `sharedWitnesses`, then higher confidence, then the positive point over a zero point; (5) if both are weak with zero witnesses (no information in either direction) return `FrontierJoinEstimate.unavailable(CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE)` — a typed unknown — instead of a NONE zero. Consumers already handle typed unavailability: LmdbStorageEstimatorEvidence.joinEvidence (:241-266) returns empty and the packed cost model falls back to its independence/transition estimate (`mappedJoin == null` :313-314). Add the same precise guard in FrontierMappedStatistics.estimateJoin (:476-478): when the omni estimate is non-exact with `pointRows()==0 && confidence()==0` and no center estimate exists, return CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE. Work doubles only in the weak case and is bounded by 3.6.6b's budget shared across both orientations.

files.change: Evaluate both orientations unless forward is exact; deterministic quality-ordered selection; typed unavailable when both are zero-witness weak; carry witness/weak flags out of sampledJoinEstimate.
Never return a weak zero-point omni bridge as NONE when centers are unavailable.

findings.title: Unbounded per-estimate planning work in Omni bridge estimation (123 ms for one 2-pattern join)
findings.recommendationReason: Confirmed 123 ms per estimate on a 100 k-row synthetic store; the packed planner issues many join estimates per query and 3.6.5 adds a second orientation in the weak case, so a work bound is required to keep planning time bounded. Leaves and paths already have bounds; bridges are the gap.
findings.rootCause: FrontierOmniIndex.estimateBridge (:797-909) and estimateCompositeBridge (:712-783) scan the sampled side with `scanLane(plane, lane, sampled, consumer, scratch)` (:1038-1041 -> `maximumCandidateRows = Integer.MAX_VALUE`), collecting up to MAXIMUM_JOIN_KEYS=4 096 keys per lane (:23), then issue one `estimateSingleLaneDetailed` (:1118-1135) per key per plane, each a full `scanLane` over the candidate cell (up to `witnessCeilingPerCell`=8 192 rows) — worst case lanes(4)·planes(2)·4 096·8 192 ≈ 2.7e8 row visits per estimate. `Scratch.recordCandidateRows` (:1436-1440) accumulates `candidateRowsVisited` but nothing reads it (no callers of `candidateRowsVisited()` in the package). By contrast `estimatePlane` (:985-1037) scans leaves progressively by priority tier (INITIAL_LEAF_PRIORITY_TIER=64, doubling while weak) and path programs enforce MAXIMUM_PATH_WORK=262 144 (:405, :444). The cost model's `initializeLineageWorkBudget` (LmdbPackedCostModel:3778-3788) bounds the *number* of lineage estimates, not work per estimate.
findings.fix: (1) Per-estimate budget in `Scratch`: add `long remainingCandidateRows`; `beginEstimate(long budget)` called at the top of `estimateJoin`/`estimateSubgraph` (and `estimateLeaf` for symmetry) with MAXIMUM_BRIDGE_WORK = 262 144 (same order as MAXIMUM_PATH_WORK); `recordCandidateRows` decrements; `scanLane(..., maximumCandidateRows)` uses `min(requested, remaining)` and, when `remaining == 0`, returns the current progressive (weak) LaneEstimate instead of scanning further. (2) Progressive sampled-side scan in both bridges: start at INITIAL_BRIDGE_PRIORITY_TIER (256 rows) per lane and double while `sampledJoinEstimate`'s quality is weak and budget remains — the key map then holds ≤ tier keys, which bounds degree probes; `restrictPrefixSampling` already yields the correct inclusion probability for prefix samples (:1093-1096). (3) Degree probes: `estimateSingleLaneDetailed(probe, lane, scratch, DEGREE_PROBE_ROWS=1 024)` using the existing progressive `scanLane` semantics (note `progressive` requires `deltaIndex.isEmpty()` at :1093; when deltas are present fall back to the budget cap only). (4) The budget is shared by both orientations from 3.6.5 so the total per estimate stays bounded. (5) Expose `Scratch.candidateRowsVisited()` through FrontierStatisticsView/Lease for tests (package-private). Accuracy: when cheap, scans still reach exact/complete cells as today (the tier grows until strong); only pathological sizes are truncated into wider intervals.

findings.title: Stale-generation window between LMDB commit and recordStoreCommit lets new snapshots read stale exact counts as authoritative
findings.recommendationReason: Mechanism is unambiguous in the code and the guard is tiny and precise; the full sequence-keyed fix belongs to wp8's txn plumbing.
findings.rootCause: LmdbSailStore.flush (:2320-2367): `tripleStore.commit()` (:2334, or via the async worker) makes epoch E+1 visible before `statisticsService.recordStoreCommit(E+1, seq')` runs at :2360-2362 (and `appendCurrentFrontierMutationTail` at :2363). A reader opening a snapshot in that window calls LmdbStatisticsService.acquire(E+1) (:183-197): the staleness test is `snapshotEpoch > coveredEpoch && (latestStoreSequence < 0 || latestStoreSequence > coveredSequence)`; `latestStoreSequence` still equals `coveredSequence`, so the condition is false and a READY lease on the generation that lacks the new rows is returned with fallbackReason NONE. `estimateLeaf(E+1, …)` (:275-277) fails the `snapshotEpoch == latestStoreEpoch` tail check and also lands in `acquire`. The same window exists for metadata-only epoch advances (`acknowledgeFrontierCoverage` :692-700 records after the ack write txn). Not reproduced by a test (timing window), but the code path is deterministic.
findings.fix: Precise guard in `acquire(long snapshotEpoch)`: if `latestStoreEpoch >= 0 && snapshotEpoch > latestStoreEpoch` (the service has been told about at least one commit and this snapshot is newer than anything it knows) return `FrontierStatisticsLease.unavailable(CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE)`; with 3.6.1 the planner falls back to storage evidence for the microsecond window instead of stale exact counts. The `latestStoreEpoch >= 0` condition keeps the many FrontierStatisticsBuilderTest/repro tests that call `service.estimateJoin(snapshot.snapshotEpoch(), …)` without `recordStoreCommit` valid; production always records at open (LmdbSailStore:443). Full fix (cross-WP, wp8): key `acquire`/`openView` on the journal sequence read inside the same read txn (`TripleStore.latestFrontierMutationSequence(Txn)` :2431 already exists) so coverage checks stop depending on recordStoreCommit ordering.

files.change: Add `latestStoreEpoch >= 0 && snapshotEpoch > latestStoreEpoch -> CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE` before the existing staleness test.

additionalTests: LmdbStatisticsServiceTest: publish (covered epoch 5, seq 10), `recordStoreCommit(5,10,…)`; `acquire(6)` -> not ready (CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE); after `recordStoreCommit(6,12,…)` + `installMutationTail` -> `estimateLeaf(6, probe)` uses the tail overlay; `acquire(5)` still READY.
LmdbStatisticsServiceTest: with `latestStoreEpoch == -1` (never recorded) `acquire(any epoch within [baseEpoch, coveredEpoch])` unchanged (builder-test compatibility).

findings.title: Fast-AGMS 'upper' is not a bound (all-zero lanes -> point 0, upper 1, confidence 0.86)
findings.recommendationReason: The repro `rareSharedKeysExplicitPlaneAgmsFallbackKeepsExactInsideInterval` passed (worstQ 8.6, none excluded) and the fallback is reachable only for EXPLICIT-plane predicate-only probes, so the dangerous case was not reproduced; but the zero-lane arithmetic is verifiably wrong and a one-line typed guard removes it without touching the healthy path.
findings.rootCause: FrontierMappedStatistics.estimateJoin AGMS branch (:496-524): `lanes[lane] = max(0, dot)`; `point = median`; `upper = min(productBound, 4·max(point, laneUpper) + 1)`; confidence `1 - exp(-lanes/2)` ≈ 0.86 for 4 lanes. When every lane's signed dot product is ≤ 0 (noise-dominated regime) the result is `[0, 1]` with 0.86 confidence and fallbackReason NONE — an interval that excludes any positive true size while claiming confidence. The shape check `agmsShape(probe)` (predicate in the heavy list of every probed plane) is why BOTH_PLANES probes on stores without inferred rows never reach it.
findings.fix: Guard: if `laneUpper <= 0.0` (no lane observed positive mass) return `FrontierJoinEstimate.unavailable(CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE)` (typed unknown; consumers fall back to independence). Optionally make the upper a real bound: AGMS median-of-lanes error is bounded by `c·sqrt(F2(L)·F2(R)/width)`; compute the second moments from the same `agmsCounter` sums (sum of squares per lane) and set `upper = min(productBound, point + 4·sqrt(F2L·F2R/width))`, `lower = max(0, point − same)`, confidence scaled by `min(1, point / error)`. The second part is medium-sized and should be validated with the repro's disjoint-heavy-hitter datasets before landing.

files.change: Typed unavailable when no lane has positive mass; optional F2-based error bound.

additionalTests: FrontierMappedStatistics unit test with a synthetic generation whose AGMS shards produce all-zero dot products -> fallbackReason CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE, never `[0,1]` with confidence 0.86.

sharedInfrastructure: Three small shared pieces. (1) `LmdbFrontierLeafAnswer` (new, core/sail/lmdb/.../lmdb/): the single predicate "Frontier answered authoritatively for this probe" (mode == AUTHORITATIVE && fallbackReason == NONE && finite point) and the roadmap 4.3 fallback chain Frontier -> bounded page/B-tree estimate (STORAGE_SUMMARY) -> exact count only in the decision tier -> total-rows ceiling, implemented once in LmdbStorageEstimatorEvidence and reused by the packed path via LmdbEstimatorRuntime.conventionalStatementPatternRows and by LmdbEstimatorStorageAccess.packedStatementPatternRows; it also decides SHADOW behaviour. wp6 (LEO) should use the same predicate when deciding whether feedback targets mapped or scalar evidence, and §3.8 cost-model work should read the same fallback reason to apply quantile costing. (2) `FrontierStatisticsException.permanent`/`requiresBaseRebuild()` + `LmdbSailStore.classifyDeltaFailure` + `FrontierRebuildSchedulePolicy`: typed failure classification and debounce-with-deadline scheduling for the whole Frontier lifecycle; any future publication path (compaction, dimension migration) should throw typed permanent failures rather than IOException. (3) `FrontierOmniIndex.Scratch` per-estimate work budget (`beginEstimate`, `remainingCandidateRows`) shared by leaf, bridge (both orientations), star and path estimators — the cost model's lineage work budget bounds estimate *count*; this bounds work *per estimate*.

§3.3 plan caches (wp3): plans built during a cold phase now use STORAGE_SUMMARY evidence; `LmdbPackedCostModel.providerVersion()` (:182-189) mixes mode/dataset flags but not Frontier READY state, and `validateStalePlan` (:172-180) replans with reason 'frontier-statistics-unavailable' — verify that PackedPlanCache invalidates cold-planned entries once Frontier becomes READY, otherwise 3.6.1 makes cold plans stickier. Also `LmdbStorageEstimatorEvidence` candidate freshness/`snapshotVersion` is the 3.3.3 restart-version bug's input.

LmdbEstimatorArchitectureTest (repo-wide guard, not a WP): LmdbStorageEstimatorEvidence is at 697/700 lines; the new helper must be added to ROOT_IMPLEMENTATIONS and must not reference LmdbEstimationEngine/LmdbEstimatorRuntime; new files need the exact copyright header and agent signature.

Benchmarks/ITs: QueryBenchmarkTest and LmdbThemeQueryRegressionIT await READY through LmdbPlannerAwait.awaitLmdbOptimizerPipeline (which calls `rebuildFrontierStatistics()`), so warm expectations are unaffected; cold-phase plan fingerprints (if any are recorded) will change after 3.6.1.
openQuestions: 3.6.3: is it safe to start a base rebuild while `storeTxnStarted` is true (write txn open)? The rebuild reads an LMDB MVCC snapshot and `acknowledgeFrontierMutationsThrough` uses the independent-writer gate designed for this, but the guard exists at :1174 and `rebuildFrontierStatistics()` throws at :638 when a write txn is active; the design keeps the guard and applies the deadline only to the quiet period. A long-running writer can still starve the rebuild.

3.6.4: retention depth — current + direct predecessor (required by `rollback()`/recovery) is proposed; should more history be kept for forensic/rollback purposes, and should the startup sweep be opt-in for the first release?

3.6.2: the delta-tier rebuild fraction (0.75 of `deltaAndManifestBudgetBytes`) and the transient-retry bound (8) are constants; should either be exposed in LmdbStoreConfig? Also whether to derive delta-build dimensions from the manifest (avoiding a rebuild on -Xmx change) or simply rebuild.
3.6.1: should STORAGE_SUMMARY evidence used while Frontier is unavailable be stamped so plan caches replan when READY (depends on the §3.3 fix design)?

3.6.6b: budget/tier constants (262 144 candidate rows, 256-row initial bridge tier, 1 024-row degree probes) need validation on the LMDB theme benchmark harness before landing; a `-Dfrontier.bridge.work` system property for experiments only (not a behaviour flag) may be acceptable.

Where to place the slow reproducers (39-48 s each): module unit suite under the `slowTestsOnly` profile vs Failsafe IT; the repo's no-red-baseline policy requires them to be green before merge either way.
